key_insight: Cr₃C₂–Ti-DLC thin-film coatings reduced tool degradation by 26% for H13 steel and 23% for WC–10% Co during dissimilar friction stir welding.
engineering_relevance: The coatings offer a route to improved tool durability when joining AA6022-T4 aluminum to galvanized DP600 steel.
method: Compare coated and uncoated H13 steel and WC–10% Co tools in dissimilar friction stir welding.
Measure weld surface finish with 3D white-light interferometry and thermal profiles with infrared thermography.
Assess tool degradation using optical microscopy, SEM–EDS, and weight-loss measurements.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative degradation reductions and identifies thread flattening, micro-abrasion, and material pickup on uncoated H13 tools.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish coating durability over extended production runs or quantify coating cost-effectiveness.
paper_title: Performance of Cr 3 C 2 -Ti-DLC coated tools in dissimilar friction stir welding
